Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  Fed on hold / bull flattening
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  ECB on hold / rotation winner
🇨🇳 China  Bearish  easing bias / weak demand
🇦🇺 Australia  Mixed  hawkish hold after hike
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  easing ahead / strong growth
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Guidance beats the quarter: buy physical-AI bottlenecks, sell beats without raises
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Grid, cable and copper supply behind the data-centre build
European defence production financed by the EU
Bitcoin trades like a software stock; wait for the reclaim before adding
Bonds bid, dollar soft, credit wobbling at the AI issuers
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
FOMC minutes and delayed data: how many cuts are left in the curve
US–Iran talks: is the oil risk premium being priced out too early
$NVDA  Feb. 25 print with Meta volumes locked in  ↑
$WMT  holiday-week print tests the defensive premium  →
Strategy / MSTR  "leveraged bitcoin and a 65% option yield"
Hims & Hers / HIMS  "a squeeze bet against the Wegovy showdown"
Silver / SLV  "a retail rally turning into liquidation"
body: Wednesday, February 18 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Labour data are holding up while headline inflation cools, leaving the Fed comfortably on hold. January payrolls rose by 130,000 and unemployment fell to 4.3%, January CPI rose 2.4%, less than expected, and the ISM manufacturing PMI printed 52.6%. The soft spot is the consumer, with December retail sales flat. Barr sees the Fed on hold for some time, while Goolsbee sees 'several' cuts if inflation gets on track to 2%.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.43% and the 10Y at 4.05%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +62 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 16 bps and the 10Y 19 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more), leaving the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17). Barron's reports Treasury yields at 2026 lows. The S&P 500 closed at 6,843.22, down 1.75% over five sessions, and the VIX at 20.29, up 27.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

New / Most Important: The driver is AI-capex anxiety, not the cycle: BofA's fund manager survey shows worry over the capex race at a record high, even as Nvidia sells Meta millions of chips in a multiyear deal. The market is repricing who pays for AI versus who gets paid, which is why the VIX rose while yields fell.

Playbook ✓: Own duration (IEF, TLT) and equal-weight cyclicals; underweight mega-cap capex spenders and long-duration software. Add 2Y on any hawkish read of the FOMC minutes, which markets await alongside GDP. Change the call if core inflation re-accelerates or the VIX falls back toward its 20-session-ago 15.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

Macro Stance: Europe is the main beneficiary of the rotation out of US mega-cap tech: the STOXX 600 closed at 621.29, up 3.07% over 20 sessions, and the FTSE 100 at 10,556.20, up 4.24% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Europe and Asia led equity fund inflows while the US recorded a weekly outflow.

Activity & Inflation: Euro-zone inflation fell to 1.7% in January, letting the ECB extend its longest pause since the negative-rate era. Germany lags, with the DAX up only 1.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). UK unemployment hit a five-year high of 5.2%, pushing the Bank of England toward cuts.

New / Most Important: The FT reported that Lagarde will leave the ECB before the end of her term, opening a succession contest while EUR/USD sits at 1.1850, up 1.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). A more hawkish successor would be mainly a currency risk for exporters.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight European large caps versus the Nasdaq 100, favouring UK domestics and banks that gain from a lower Bank Rate, with a partial EUR/USD hedge for the succession risk. Downgrade to Mixed if the STOXX 600 gives back its 20-session gain or flows into Europe reverse.

Macro Stance: China starts the Year of the Horse with policy rhetoric shifting to consumption but no demand turn in the data. Xi prioritised 'AI-plus' and consumer spending to counter economic risks, yet the January numbers show contracting factories, a credit miss and falling home prices. The macro stance stays bearish even as Hong Kong equities hold up on flows.

PMIs & Activity: The January official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3, back in contraction, while a private survey showed factory expansion accelerating in January. That split favours export-oriented private manufacturers over the state-heavy domestic economy. The February official PMI is the next confirmation point; a return above 50 would be needed to soften the view.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists, so the seasonal credit surge was smaller than hoped. January CPI rose just 0.2%, which keeps real borrowing costs high for a deflation-prone economy. What would change the view is a sustained beat in household lending alongside firmer core prices.

Property: Housing has not found a floor: SCMP reports home prices keep falling despite policy support. Without stable prices, households keep paying down mortgages rather than borrowing, which is consistent with the weak loan demand. Confirmation of a bottom would require consecutive months of flat new-home prices in the largest cities.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The external front is calmer: Reuters reported that Trump paused China tech bans ahead of a Xi summit, lowering the near-term export-control risk for Chinese tech and for US chip suppliers. Domestically, Xi's emphasis on consumption and 'AI-plus' points to targeted support for services and technology rather than a broad infrastructure stimulus.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng closed at 26,705.94 in its last session before the holiday, up 0.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-16), capping what SCMP called Hong Kong's best lunar-year performance in eight years. The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,082.07, down 0.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). US-listed proxies are weaker: ASHR closed at 33.86 (+0.89% over 20 sessions), FXI at 38.52 (-1.98%) and KWEB at 32.72 (-8.37%), while USD/CNY stood at 6.9080, down 0.86% over 20 sessions as the yuan firmed (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

New / Most Important: The most important change is the tone of US–China relations: the tech-ban pause ahead of a Xi summit takes a key tail risk off the table. Combined with a firmer yuan, it gives Beijing room to ease without currency pressure, but the January credit miss shows easing is not yet reaching borrowers.

Playbook ✓: Underweight broad China beta (FXI, KWEB) until the official PMI regains 50 and household credit improves; express the AI-plus and services theme only through Hong Kong-listed leaders on pullbacks, and avoid developers while prices keep falling. ⚠ Divergence: Hong Kong's best lunar-year run in eight years contradicts the weak PMI and credit data — flows are front-running a policy turn the numbers do not yet show.

Macro Stance: Japan's domestic growth is thin but the external engine is strong: Q4 GDP grew an annualised 0.2%, below expectations, while January exports surged nearly 17% on soaring shipments to China. The IMF urged Japan to keep raising rates and avoid cutting the sales tax, which supports gradual BOJ normalisation under Takaichi.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 153.609, up 0.54% in the prior session but down 2.89% over 20 sessions, and the Nikkei 225 closed at 56,566.49, down 0.42% on the day but up 5.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). A firmer yen alongside rising equities says foreign money is buying Japan's reform-and-reflation story rather than the weak-yen export trade.

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japanese equities, tilted to banks and domestic demand that benefit from higher BOJ rates, and fade USD/JPY rallies toward its 20-session-ago level of 158.177 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Turn neutral if weak GDP spreads into wages, or if fiscal expansion pushes long JGB yields into the kind of disorderly rise the IMF warning is meant to prevent.

Macro Stance: The RBA hiked in February, and the minutes show a material shift in inflation risks behind the move. The bank also says there is no set path for future rates, so the market is pricing a hawkish hold rather than a hiking cycle, with the skew toward one more move rather than cuts.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7073, up 5.41% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 at 8,958.90, up 0.95% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Banks carry the index, with NAB hitting a record high on robust first-quarter cash profit, and BHP's profit beat as copper overtook iron ore earnings on AI-driven demand.

Playbook ✓: Stay long AUD against USD while the RBA keeps its hawkish bias, but hold ASX exposure neutral: banks are priced for record results and the strong currency trims miners' earnings. Prefer copper-heavy miners over energy producers. Turn bearish on the AUD if the next CPI cools enough to make February's hike look like a one-off.

Monetary & Activity: Poland pairs the region's strongest growth with inflation at target: GDP growth accelerated to 4% (Bankier: 'PKB przyspieszył do 4 procent' — GDP sped up to 4 percent), and January CPI came in at 2.2% y/y. The print was above forecasts, but commentators see the MPC moving closer to a March cut (300Gospodarka: 'RPP bliżej marcowej obniżki stóp').

FX & Markets: EUR/PLN closed at 4.2131 and USD/PLN at 3.5548, down 1.96% over 20 sessions, while EPOL closed at 37.50 (+4.4% over 20 sessions, -3.25% over five) and the WIG20TR ETF at 66.06 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Polish bond yields fell below 5%, the lowest in two years (Bankier). Pekao is up 7.99% and PGE 14.93% over 20 sessions, while KGHM fell 6.46% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

Companies: KGHM signed a EUR 6 billion copper agreement with Denmark's NKT, yet the shares fell alongside silver, a sign the stock trades on precious-metal prices before contracts. For banks, the CJEU ruling means WIBOR 'will not be a second Swiss franc' (Rzeczpospolita: 'WIBOR nie będzie drugim frankiem'), removing a large legal tail risk; PKO BP closed at 89.20, up 2.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

Security & New Development: The EU approved €44 billion in SAFE defence loans for Poland, financing a procurement wave that favours local production. The flip side is a wider deficit, so the bond rally depends on inflation staying at target.

Playbook ✓: Own Polish banks (PKO, Pekao) and PGE as the growth, March-cut and WIBOR-relief trade; underweight KGHM until silver stabilises. Keep zloty exposure unhedged while yields stay below 5%. ⚠ Divergence: January inflation came in above forecasts while the market leans into a March cut — a second upside surprise would force a front-end repricing and hit the rate-sensitive rally.

Narrative: Consensus has flipped from 'AI lifts all tech' to 'AI eats software': XLK closed at 139.48, down 4.22% over 20 sessions, with Oracle down 19.43% and Palantir down 22.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Forbes tied the latest leg to Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 release.

Reported: Palo Alto Networks cut its annual profit forecast as deal costs bite, and the shares fell — the group's template of decent quarters, weaker outlooks and lower prices. Apple was the exception, up 3.17% to 263.88 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Microsoft, at 396.86 and down 13.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), was dumped despite the largest earnings beat in its history. With estimates intact and the price reset, it has the most room for a positive surprise among the mega caps.

⚡ Breaking Convention: When a record beat is sold and one model release moves a whole sector, positioning rather than earnings is setting prices — the precondition for a capitulation low. The first software name that beats and rallies would signal the discount is closing.

Narrative: Communication services split between AI spenders and ad platforms exposed to AI disruption: XLC closed at 114.40, down 0.67% over 20 sessions, with Meta up 3.07% but Alphabet down 8.48% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Meta's multiyear deal for millions of Nvidia chips shows spend is still escalating.

Reported: Pinterest forecast downbeat revenue as it battles for digital ad dollars, and the shares plunged; ad budgets are concentrating in the largest AI-enabled platforms. Disney closed at 105.44, down 5.18% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Netflix is the de-rated candidate for an upside surprise, closing at 77.00, down 12.5% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Its subscription revenue is not obviously threatened by AI tools, so a steady print would stand out.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Alphabet's 100-year sterling bond is raising fears of a debt-fuelled AI arms race. If investors start valuing hyperscalers like capital-intensive utilities, the sector multiple compresses even while revenue grows.

Narrative: Financials sit between solid bank fundamentals and AI contagion in fee businesses: XLF closed at 52.20, down 4.11% over 20 sessions but up 1.06% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). A positively sloped curve at +62 bps still supports net interest margins (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17).

Reported: Bank prints were strong, led by NAB's record high on robust cash profit, and JPMorgan rose 1.51% to 307.13 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The weakness sits in brokers and alternative managers rather than lenders.

EPS Upside Watch: Morgan Stanley named Citigroup its top bank stock pick, a restructuring story with trading and lending leverage. Capital-markets franchises also gain from heavy tech debt issuance and higher volatility.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The risk sits in private credit, not banks: Bloomberg says private credit's software bet is even bigger than it appears. If AI impairs software cash flows, losses surface first at direct lenders and alternative managers.

Narrative: Energy has been the rotation's biggest winner: XLE closed at 53.75, up 12.71% over 20 sessions, far ahead of Brent at $67.42, up 5.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). That gap is stretched as the geopolitical premium fades, with oil at a two-week low on talk of progress in US-Iran talks.

Reported: TotalEnergies cut buybacks as profit slipped on lower oil prices, showing capital returns are the first casualty of cheaper crude. Exxon fell 1.52% and Chevron 1.74% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: With WTI at $62.33, down 3.15% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), estimates are more likely to drift lower than higher. Only refiners and gas-weighted producers with volume growth look set up for beats.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The tail risk runs the other way: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz for live-fire drills while talking to the US. A breakdown would gap crude higher, but energy equities, up far more than crude, have already priced much of that upside.

Narrative: Industrials are where the rotation lands with earnings support: XLI closed at 175.08, up 4.9% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar at 764.76, up 18.22% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Data-centre construction feeds directly into power equipment and machinery.

Reported: Siemens shares jumped on a lifted outlook and a market-view beat, the cleanest example of the market paying for guidance. GE closed at 327.08, up 3.7% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Grid equipment makers have the most visible order books: Exelon's capital plan reached $41.3 billion on transmission, and those dollars flow to turbines, switchgear and cable suppliers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Not every industrial is an AI winner: labour-heavy logistics faces automation risk while machinery makers sell into the build-out. Own equipment and electrical names and avoid asset-light freight brokers even as the ETF rallies.

Narrative: Discretionary is the weak link: XLY closed at 116.04, down 5.12% over 20 sessions, with Amazon down 15.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Amazon is priced as an AI spender rather than a retailer, and December retail sales were unexpectedly flat.

Reported: McDonald's beat global sales estimates as its value bets paid off: consumers are spending, but on value. Home Depot fell 2.05% to 383.04 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Value formats have the best setup, given McDonald's evidence that value drives traffic. Nike, up 2.68% in the prior session but only 0.68% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), is the turnaround name where low expectations make a modest beat count.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Falling yields have not lifted housing-linked retail: Home Depot is up just 0.75% over 20 sessions while the 10Y fell 19 bps (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17). Discretionary earnings now lean on the labour market alone.

Narrative: Staples have been the defensive winner: XLP closed at 88.20, up 7.42% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 7.64% and Costco up 5.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The bid is as much about falling bond yields as about earnings.

Reported: General Mills cut its sales forecast and food stocks tumbled; XLP fell 1.46% and Walmart 3.76% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The warning shows packaged-food pricing power is exhausted.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart is the sector's swing print, at the centre of the Reuters week-ahead; its scale lets it gain share as weaker brands lose shelf space. Costco, at 1,012.05, is the other structural share-taker (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The defensive bid is not a fundamental bid: the group's own news flow is weak, and staples trade as bond proxies. A back-up in the 10Y from 4.05% would hit them regardless of earnings (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17).

Narrative: Healthcare is flat-lining: XLV closed at 157.37, up 1.05% over 20 sessions, with Eli Lilly at 1,036.05 (-0.23%) and UnitedHealth down 12.67% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Drug-pricing policy and managed-care cost trends cap the multiple, so the sector is not acting as a defensive refuge.

Reported: Medtronic's unchanged annual outlook clouded upbeat quarterly results, a textbook case of the market ignoring the beat and selling the guide. UnitedHealth closed at 289.09, down 1.4% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Obesity-drug volume remains the main estimate driver for Lilly, which has held flat while the market fell. Managed care, with UnitedHealth up 4.86% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), is the rebound candidate if medical-cost trends stabilise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Hedge funds bet big against Hims & Hers before the Wegovy showdown: the crowd expects branded obesity drugs to squeeze the telehealth channel. An outcome favouring telehealth would hit both that consensus and branded-price expectations at once.

Narrative: Materials lead on copper and gold: XLB closed at 52.70, up 8.26% over 20 sessions, with Newmont up 7.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). BHP's profit beat as copper overtook iron ore earnings on AI-driven demand, confirming copper as the data-centre and grid metal.

Reported: Antofagasta's profit jumped 52% on record copper prices, showing the big miners' earnings mix shifting toward electrification metals. Freeport closed at 61.09, up 4.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Gold miners carry the most operating leverage: gold closed at $4,905.90, up 6.76% over 20 sessions despite a 2.78% drop in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), so Q1 realised prices support estimate upgrades for low-cost producers.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Physical copper is loosening: global exchange stocks topped 1 million tonnes for the first time in 21 years, and copper fell 5.25% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The AI-demand story is right on direction but early on timing, so low-cost miners beat the metal itself.

Narrative: Real estate is the cleanest beneficiary of the bull flattening: XLRE closed at 43.94, up 4.0% over five sessions and 4.1% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), as Treasury yields hit 2026 lows.

Reported: The feed carries few US REIT prints in this window, so the sector's news is macro. A 10Y down 19 bps over 20 observations lowers cap-rate pressure and refinancing costs (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Healthcare, data-centre and industrial REITs with contracted rent escalators gain most from lower funding costs. The 30Y at 4.68% is the funding benchmark to watch for long-lease landlords (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The AI scare trade wiped billions from commercial real estate stocks and spread to office REITs. AI-driven white-collar job fears are a new demand risk for office space that falling yields cannot fix, so own the rate trade through non-office REITs.

Narrative: Utilities are the preferred AI-power proxy with a bond-like floor: XLU closed at 46.38, up 6.67% over five sessions and 6.89% over 20, while Constellation rose 11.34% and Vistra 13.54% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Exelon's capital plan reached $41.3 billion on transmission.
Reported: Constellation rose 5.05% in the prior session to 303.01 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), as regulated peers keep lifting multi-year capex plans on data-centre load.

EPS Upside Watch: Grid-heavy regulated names with contracted large loads have the most visible rate-base growth; NextEra closed at 92.71, up 10.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Falling Treasury yields add a valuation tailwind on top of the earnings growth.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Affordability politics is the counter-signal: electricity prices are rising at double the rate of inflation, and analysts see no relief from data-centre demand. Regulators may cap allowed returns or push costs onto data-centre owners, so allowed returns, not load growth, are the variable to watch.

Narrative: European autos are rallying on restructuring hopes rather than demand: the STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts tracker closed at 46.40, up 4.41% over 20 sessions, with Volkswagen preference shares up 6.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Volkswagen plans to cut costs by 20% by end-2028, Manager Magazin reports.

Reported: Mercedes' 2025 earnings more than halved as it took a $1.2 billion hit from tariffs. Mercedes-Benz shares nonetheless rose 2.1% in the prior session to 58.86 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), a sign the bad news was priced.

EPS Upside Watch: Cost-cutters have the upside, with Volkswagen's plan the biggest self-help lever in the sector. Stellantis announces full-year 2025 results on February 26, the next hard test of the reset.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Stellantis is up 7.11% over five sessions but down 18.44% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17): relief rallies in the most damaged names are outpacing the quality OEMs. That looks like short-covering rather than a demand recovery, and it reverses if tariff costs keep rising.

Narrative: Semis are the part of AI that still gets paid: SOXX closed at 354.10, up 3.4% over 20 sessions, with TSMC ADRs up 6.37% and Micron up 10.21% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Bloomberg reports AI demand is causing a critical memory-chip shortage, and Meta's multiyear chip deal underwrites accelerator demand.

Reported: Applied Materials gave a rosy forecast as AI and memory boost demand, and equipment and memory have led the group since. ASML closed at 1,419.78, up 4.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

EPS Upside Watch: Nvidia's results on Feb. 25 are the sector's main estimate event; the stock closed at 184.97, down 0.68% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17), so it enters the print without its peers' rally. Memory makers have the cleanest revision path while shortage pricing persists.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AMD closed at 203.08, down 12.4% over 20 sessions, while Micron rose 10.21% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The market now pays for scarce memory and equipment rather than accelerator challengers, so a blanket 'buy semis' call misses the dispersion.

Rewarded: Guidance raisers in physical bottlenecks were rewarded: Siemens jumped on a lifted outlook, Applied Materials gave a rosy AI and memory forecast, and NAB hit a record on robust cash profit. McDonald's value-led sales beat showed that consumers reward price and investors reward the companies that capture it.

Punished: Beats with flat or light guidance were sold: Medtronic fell on an unchanged outlook, Palo Alto slid after cutting its annual profit forecast, and Pinterest plunged on a downbeat revenue forecast. Microsoft is still being sold despite the largest earnings beat in its history.

Pattern: The market is paying for the durability of earnings, not the quarter. It discounts any business whose terminal value AI could compress — software seats, ad networks, brokers — and pays for physical scarcity in memory, equipment, power and metals. Beats are necessary but not sufficient; the raise is what moves the stock.

Attention into EPS: Attention now concentrates on Walmart, the focus of the Reuters week-ahead, and on Nvidia's results on Feb. 25. In Europe, Stellantis's full-year results on February 26 test whether the autos rally has substance.

Playbook: Buy post-print dips in guidance raisers tied to physical AI supply chains, and fade beats that come without a raise, especially in software and ad-tech. Into prints, use defined-risk option spreads where 'beat and fall' has been the rule. Revisit if two large software names beat and rally in a row, which would mark the end of the AI-disruption discount.

Attention Gap: Investors debate hyperscaler capex, but far less attention goes to the suppliers that capex must pass through. KGHM's EUR 6 billion copper agreement with NKT, Exelon's $41.3 billion transmission-led plan and BHP's copper-led earnings point to multi-year order books that sit outside the AI-software debate.

Exposure & Risk: Express through power generators and utilities with transmission exposure, such as CEG at 303.01 and VST at 173.68, plus copper producers such as FCX at 61.09 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). The main risk is affordability politics: electricity prices rising at double the rate of inflation could cap allowed returns.

Attention Gap: Defence attention sits on US primes, while the new money is EU-financed European production: the EU approved €44 billion of SAFE loans for Poland alone. Procurement tied to EU loans favours European and local manufacturing, a demand stream that is barely visible in US-centric defence screens.

Exposure & Risk: Express through a European aerospace-and-defence basket weighted to munitions and air defence rather than US primes. Risk: a Russia–Ukraine ceasefire would hit sentiment before it touches order books, which run on multi-year EU-financed budgets; slow EU disbursement is the second risk.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was $67,494.22, down 1.96% on the day and 24.32% over 20 sessions; ether closed at $1,992.19 (-33.74% over 20 sessions) and solana at $85.20, up 8.74% over five sessions but down 31.91% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). IBIT closed at 38.39, down 29.22% over 20 sessions, Coinbase at 166.02 (-31.15%) and Strategy at 128.67, down 3.89% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

New / Most Important: Corporate buyers are still adding: Strategy added 2,486 bitcoin last week. But bitcoin is now trading with the AI-exposed, long-duration parts of the equity market rather than as a hedge against them, and IBIT's 29.22% 20-session drop shows ETF holders absorbing losses (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17). Until that correlation breaks, crypto is a leveraged expression of the software sell-off.

Playbook: Stay underweight until bitcoin reclaims $70,000, the level it clawed back to after an $8.7 billion wipeout; a daily close above it would turn the call neutral. Prefer IBIT over MSTR and COIN, whose leverage to the bitcoin price cuts both ways, and avoid alt-coins until ether stops underperforming bitcoin.

Rates & Dollar: TLT closed at 89.87, up 2.69% over five sessions, and IEF at 97.20, as the 10Y yield fell 17 bps over five observations to 4.05% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17). Barron's reports Treasury yields at 2026 lows. The DXY closed at 97.16, down 2.24% over 20 sessions but up 0.29% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

Credit Check: HYG closed at 80.81, down 0.35% over 20 sessions, while LQD rose 1.02% to 111.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17): investment grade is riding the rates rally, high yield is not. Supply is the pressure point, with Alphabet's century bond and private credit's large software exposure putting AI-linked credit at the centre of the next spread move.

Portfolio Implication: Prefer Treasuries and short-duration investment grade over high yield, and avoid private-credit vehicles heavy in software loans. Keep a modest dollar underweight via EUR and AUD. Reverse if HYG regains its 20-session-ago level of 81.09 while TLT rolls over, which would signal growth relief rather than a flight to quality (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-17).

What Is Priced: The 2Y at 3.43% sits below the 3M bill at 3.69% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-17), so the front end already prices cuts within a year. Markets are waiting on the FOMC minutes and US GDP, with Fed speakers split between Goolsbee's conditional 'several cuts' and Barr's on-hold message.

Conditional Expression: If the minutes lean dovish and inflation stays on track, extend duration via IEF and add rate-sensitive XLRE. If they echo Barr's patience, the front end sells off: reduce 2Y exposure, trim XLRE and keep the dollar short only against EUR.
